title: Rabbi Zekharyah ben Kevutal
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a great man in Temple times, as in [Mishnah Yoma 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Yoma.1.6), where he said: “Many times I read before him (before the High Priest on the night of Yom Kippur) from Daniel.” Hyman argues that this does not prove that he was a Kohen, for in the Mishnah there they said that if the High Priest cannot expound, Torah scholars expound before him; so he could even be an Israelite. But from [Berakhot 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.63a.24), where they said that the sages sent to Chananya, the nephew of Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Yose ben Kifar and the son of Rabbi Zekharyah ben Kevutal, and he proclaimed concerning them that they were the great men of the generation and their fathers had served in the Temple — Hyman infers from this that he was a Kohen.

In [Yoma 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.19b.6): “Rav Chanan bar Rava taught Chiyya bar Rav: Zekharyah ben Kefutal, and Rav pointed with his hand: Kevutal.” [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.1.6.3) reads Kevutar.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Berakhot calls the emissary Zekharyah’s grandson, as does [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1139&lang=en). The Yerushalmi gives the names Kevutar and Kevutal and has Rav gesture in response to Kahana. Hyman infers priesthood from the Temple service mentioned in Berakhot.
